text:
luke (support): Heads-up — Acme Mobile reports intermittent streaming failures from our hosted API. Symptoms: client gets "Broken pipe" mid-stream, final chunk never arrives, customer says they were billed for tokens despite aborted response. They provided a curl repro and a trace id. trace: trace-7f3a9c2a link=https://internal.traces/redwood/trace-7f3a9c2a
alerts-bot: alert: spike detected on /v1/stream (5xx rate up 3.2x in 5m) — correlated traces: trace-7f3a9c2a, trace-7f3a9d10
jake (eng-oncall): Thanks — can you paste the curl repro and any gateway/nginx proxy logs? Also which model + sequence lengths? Any TLS termination in customer's proxy?
luke (support): Customer curl (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \
  -d @payload.json \
  https://api.redwood.dev/v1/stream
```
Payload includes a single long prompt, they stream client-side, then client reports ECONNRESET after ~3.2s. They said it happens ~1% of requests. They do have a mobile reverse-proxy that sits on their CDN.
jake (eng-oncall): Paste of our gateway logs for trace-7f3a9c2a: 
```
[2026-02-21T14:12:23Z] conn=172.31.9.4 trace=trace-7f3a9c2a route=/v1/stream client_close=FIN server_msgs=12 last_msg_ts=14:12:26.123 proto=HTTP/1.1
[2026-02-21T14:12:26Z] conn=172.31.9.4 trace=trace-7f3a9c2a upstream_err=EPIPE tcp_state=FIN_WAIT_2
```
sophia (devx): Two things to consider: (1) client-side half-close detection — some mobile proxies aggressively close after seeing a final chunk-size 0? (2) our billing heuristics currently mark any connection that emitted >=1 token as billable, regardless of client close reason. That explains billing complaint.
luke (support): Customer also attached a shortened client-side log: 
```
W/System: Read failed: ECONNRESET (Connection reset by peer)
stream bytes received: 1024
```
They said they did not see a trailing chunk or trailer.
jake (eng-oncall): From gateway trace we see server emitted tokens then socket got a FIN from client — but we classify socket closes that happen before server end-of-stream as 5xx if upstream reported error. Need to determine if error originates from client (client closed) vs server (internal write error). EPIPE in our logs suggests we observed a write failure. Can you repro with a synthetic client from our VPC? If we can reproduce we can isolate whether it's the mobile proxy or our runtime.
sophia (devx): Quick repro suggestion for the customer: ensure they don't close the TCP stream immediately after receiving what they think is the last chunk — wait for the connection to be idle 500ms or explicitly read until connection EOF. Also ask them to disable intermediate buffering on CDN if possible. For us, I'll add more logging around write syscall return codes and set a flag to include kernel-level errno in traces.
mina (billing): For immediate billing question: we'll temporarily suppress auto dispute for this customer until root cause is clear. Ticket: billing-4319. If this turns out to be our runtime bug we will reverse charges. Need trace ids and sample request ids.
jake (eng-oncall): I'll push a debug build to staging with extra socket write telemetry and a small tweak to the half-close heuristic (non-default, gated by env var) so we can run a canary vs their repro. Who can coordinate a short scheduled window with Acme?
luke (support): I can get them on a quick debug window tomorrow 10:00am PT. I'll collect their mobile proxy config and sample request ids.
sophia (devx): Workplan: 1) gather customer proxy config + sample curl 2) run repro from our staging with debug runtime + same client conditions 3) if repro, narrow down to kernel EPIPE vs internal queue full 4) if internal, hotfix small backoff on write flush; if client side, produce runbook for clients (keepalive, wait-for-eof) 5) billing to hold charges while under investigation
jake (eng-oncall): Also setting a short-term alert to detect large correlation of EPIPE+token-emitted so we can catch regression: rule id rb-stream-epipe-1.
luke (support): Noted. I'll open a private support ticket for Acme with billing hold and attach trace-7f3a9c2a and the curl. Will ping here once they confirm debug window. :thumbsup:
mina (billing): Added hold and note to billing-4319.
alerts-bot: incident created: rb-stream-epipe-1 (monitoring)
jake (eng-oncall): thanks all — next update after we run the staging repro. If anyone captures a kernel errno or a duplicated FIN-before-write that's the smoking gun.
luke (support): Closing thread for now, will update after the debug session.
